summary: WORKac's 8-story commercial building on Parcel B, with Breakthrough Properties assisting on the life-science real estate (SF YIMBY, 2022) and marketed as Class A office/life science after its June 2023 TCO. It houses the district's blackwater recycling plant and has since leased to the Golden State Warriors (71,000 sq ft, October 2024), Coinbase (150,000 sq ft, 2025) and Nvidia (45,000 sq ft, reported November 2025). A July 21, 2026 report (publication date) says Grey's Florals is set to open a store inside MNT Studio's space at 1090 Dr. Maya Angelou Lane in August 2026 (an announced, expected date; no opening is confirmed).

details.text: Address of Building B: the parcel's two official addresses are 1090 Dr. Maya Angelou Lane (DataSF Enterprise Addressing System address 869906) and 1089 3rd St (DataSF address 871659). SF Standard and The Real Deal (May and November 2025) also give 1090 Dr. Maya Angelou Lane; The Real Deal's October 2024 article on the Warriors lease (reposted by Mitsui Fudosan America) and The Registry's June 2021 article give 1051 3rd (Third) Street, which is not an official address for this parcel.
Developer of Building B: SF YIMBY (March 2022) names Breakthrough Properties as assisting with the life-science real estate.
Use of Building B: the Port (April 2024) says it is marketed as Class A office/life science; SF YIMBY (March 2022) said the building was expected to host a biotech company.
Building B's water recycling plant: its sewer discharge was redesigned as a force main to avoid a PG&E duct bank in Third Street.

open_questions: Construction cost: no actual or contract construction cost appears in anything read; the only figure is the $78,083,460 estimated and revised cost on the building permit, which is a filed valuation.

Groundbreaking date: no source read gives one. The Registry's June 22, 2021 article (paywalled after the lede) has a "Breaks Ground" headline, but its lede says Tishman Speyer "is planning to break ground"; the Port's December 2021 update says Parcel B "completed all necessary pile driving work" and was preparing to begin vertical construction; SF YIMBY (March 7, 2022) says "Less than three months ago, the vertical work started for the structure"; the Port's October 2023 memo lists "Commenced construction of all four Phase 1 vertical buildings" without a date.

Square footage: sources give 272,770 (SF YIMBY), 281,639 (the Port's 2019 appraisal table), 295,000 (The Real Deal), 313,952 (a Commercial Real Estate Direct repost of Commercial Property Executive) and 300,000 (ArchDaily and Hathaway Dinwiddie). The split in this record's map notes (258,994 office + 13,773 retail, which adds to 272,767) comes from a contractor page that could not be read.
Lease terms and rents for the Warriors, Coinbase and Nvidia: undisclosed in every report read.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (the parcel is part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot that Mission Rock replaces; no source read says when parking use ended) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.
When Nvidia's lease commences: The Real Deal (Nov 21, 2025) says only that it 'is slated to occupy 45,000 square feet'; no commencement date appears in any source read.

Loeb & Loeb's pages (an undated experience page and a news item dated May 27, 2025) describe a 150,000 sq ft Building B lease for 'a leading cryptocurrency company' without naming Coinbase in their text (the name appears only in the experience page's URL). The Real Deal (May 28, 2025, citing the San Francisco Business Times) names Coinbase for 150,000 sq ft at Building B.

MNT Studio is shown as open because its own Mission Rock page says 'CLASS SCHEDULE IS NOW LIVE' and that classes can be bought with a membership, two-week trial or class credit packages (page read 2026-10-12). The page gives no opening date and no 'now open' statement, and no news report or post-opening source has been read, so the studio's opening date is unknown. Grey's Florals' August 2026 opening inside MNT's space has not been confirmed.

A business registration for Fort Point Physical Therapy at 1090 Dr Maya Angelou Ln Ste E exists since 2026-07-03 (DataSF Registered Business Locations; the same owner registered a second location at 290 Division St Fl 2 the same day); no source read shows the clinic open, so it is not listed as a tenant. A booking page on Jane App lists a 'LuxFit' location at 1090 Dr Maya Angelou Ln with a contact email at fortpointpt.com, and LuxFit's own page mentions physical therapy services without naming the clinic; neither gives an opening date.

Flour + Water Pizza Shop's opening date: PMQ Pizza (April 9, 2025) says the company 'has opened' the shop, while Appetito (published 11:00 AM EDT on April 14, 2025, before the shop's 11:30 a.m. opening hour in Pacific time) says it 'has landed at Mission Rock' and gives no opening date. The sources do not agree on a day, so only April 2025 is shown.

Board of Supervisors approvals in 2018: the Notice of Determination and the Port's October 2023 memo date the Board's affirmation of the EIR certification to March 6, 2018 (Resolution 33-18 per the Port), but the Port's September 2019 report says the Board "approved the Project" on February 13, 2018 and its recitals also cite Resolution 33-18 for the Development Agreement approval in February 2018; this record shows only the March 6 EIR action.

Square footage by use: SF YIMBY gives 272,770 at topping out (230,890 office, 13,760 retail); the Port's 2019 appraisal table gives 281,639 total and 265,205 office; the Warriors release gives 295,000; the 2025 Coinbase report gives 313,952.
Warriors' space in Building B: The Real Deal gave 71,000 sq ft on two floors in October 2024 and 70,000 sq ft in its May 2025 article.
